title: Kenyan Coconut Cookies
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Coconut Cookies — crispy, golden cookies packed with desiccated coconut, fragrant with cardamom and vanilla. Inspired by the Swahili coastal love of coconut, adapted into a universally beloved baked cookie. The ideal accompaniment to Kenyan masala chai.
longDesc: Kenyan coconut cookies combine the coastal love of coconut with the universal pleasure of a well-baked biscuit. The cardamom is the Kenyan signature — lifting the coconut into something more complex and fragrant than a plain coconut cookie. They are as at home with masala chai as they are with coffee.
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line baking tray with parchment.
Mix flour, coconut, both sugars, cardamom, cinnamon, baking powder, and salt.
Combine coconut oil, eggs, and vanilla in a separate bowl.
Mix wet into dry until a soft dough forms.
Roll into walnut-sized balls. Place on tray with space between.
Flatten slightly with a fork or palm.
Bake 12—15 minutes until golden at the edges.
Cool on tray for 5 minutes — they firm up as they cool.
chefTips: Do not over-bake — they should look slightly underdone in the centre when removed.
Coconut oil solidifies when chilled — work quickly if your kitchen is cold.
The cardamom is the Kenyan signature — do not reduce it.
commonMistakes: Over-baking — very easy with coconut cookies.
Moving before cooled — they are fragile when hot.
cookingScience: Coconut oil has a different fatty acid profile from butter — its medium-chain triglycerides produce a crisper, less chewy cookie than butter-based versions. Combined with the natural fibre in the desiccated coconut, the result is a pleasantly crunchy texture.
sustainabilityTips: Coconut oil from sustainably grown Kenyan coastal coconuts.
storage: Airtight container for up to 2 weeks.
healthBenefits: Best enjoyed as an occasional treat.
culturalNote: Kenyan coconut cookies have become a café staple — the biscuit that sits in glass jars on café counters across Nairobi and is eaten in the hundreds daily with tea and coffee.
